sample.source: Five hash-verified public Open Food Facts label photos already in the local benchmark
sample.split: All five photos were previously used in OCR exploration; this is a comparative development sample, not held-out evaluation.

reconstruction: Each source photograph was prepared in browser Canvas using the production 3,000 px long-edge cap and JPEG quality 0.98. SDK polygons were grouped and converted to production-shaped OCR observations with per-token text, confidence, bounding boxes, reading order, image IDs, and a capture record, then passed to the production parser. The 0.62× median line-height row grouping matches the production fallback. Per-field stage flags check human-annotation label/value presence and parser outputs; numeric presence can be a coincidental duplicate and same-row co-occurrence does not verify column association. Region detection precision/recall and column association require independent annotations and remain unmeasured.
networkPolicy: Images were supplied from the local process to Chrome memory; only GET requests to Paddle model hosting were allowed. The harness records no image/text payloads and blocks no local research data outside the process.
limitations: Only the same five convenience-sample images (37 fields); all were previously used during OCR exploration, so no held-out score is claimed.

PP-OCRv5 is tested with its English model; PP-OCRv6 language is selected from the existing human photo annotation only for this offline comparison. Production language detection and routing are not demonstrated.
OCR output strings are processed in memory for parsing and scoring but are not persisted.
The simple row grouper can misalign adjacent columns; detection-box existence and confidence are reported separately from final parsed nutrient accuracy.
True region detection precision/recall and column association require independent region/column annotations and remain unmeasured.
JavaScript heap metrics exclude WebAssembly linear memory, browser native allocations, and potential GPU memory.
No image bytes leave the local process; only model/runtime GETs are made. This is a candidate comparison, not product integration or population-level evidence.
